notes: Test questions T1-T12 from runs/ai-analyst-shows-sql-research.md section 7, worded exactly as asked, so mark_run.py can match them by id and text.

Chat plan: every test question is its own fresh chat; there are no follow-ups, so no row has follow_up_of. T7-T12 are Repeats of T1-T6 (same wording, definition and family) asked in new fresh chats; their rivals are the T1-T6 rival rows in the same family.

'Delivered in <year>' is read as order_status = 'delivered' and purchase year, as section 7 and piece 1 define it. The delivery-date rivals (T1b, T2d, T3e, T5c, T6c) read the year from order_delivered_customer_date instead.

'Late' is fixed before the run, as piece 1: the date part of order_delivered_customer_date later than the date part of order_estimated_delivery_date (calendar-day grain). Timestamp-grain rivals (T5b, T6b) also count orders delivered on the estimated day as late. Delivered orders with no delivered customer date count as not late and stay in the denominators.

T3's primary is price plus freight_value on items of delivered orders purchased in 2017 (what customers paid), as section 7 fixes it. Rivals: price only (T3b), all statuses with and without freight (T3c, T3d), delivery year (T3e). The payments table (payment_value) is a further plausible reading but is not loaded in Dot's workspace (only orders and order items are), so it has no row.
T4's primary is every order row purchased in 2017, all statuses. Rivals: delivered only (T4b); canceled and unavailable excluded (T4c).
Rows with asked: false are computed but not asked. Date filters use string prefixes on the raw CSV text; every value is computed from the raw CSVs. reviewed_by is left for a person to set.

Four combined rivals added 31 October 2026 before review and before the run (hard rule 2), on Saurabh's instruction: T2e (freight, delivery year), T3f (price only, delivery year), T5d and T6e (timestamp grain, delivery year). Each pairs two rivals that were already in the spec separately, so an answer combining them can be marked.
